subject: social_science

concepts.title: Classification of Economic Activities
concepts.definition: Economic operations are categorized into primary extractions of natural resources, secondary processing of raw goods, and tertiary support services.
concepts.key_idea: Economic life progresses from raw natural harvesting to manufactured products enabled by service networks.
question_patterns: classify the given activity into primary, secondary, or tertiary sector
explain the difference between primary, secondary, and tertiary economic activities
identify which sector an activity like fishing, steel making, or banking belongs to
distinguish between primary and tertiary activities with examples
what type of economic activity is agriculture and why

solution_steps.action: Examine the nature of the economic activity
solution_steps.explain: Analyze whether the task involves extracting raw natural resources, manufacturing goods, or offering services.

solution_steps.action: Assign the corresponding sector category
solution_steps.explain: Classify direct resource collection as primary, resource transformation as secondary, and operational assistance as tertiary.

concepts.title: Specialized Cultivation Branches
concepts.definition: Agricultural science includes specialized branches such as sericulture, pisciculture, viticulture, and horticulture for commercial production.
concepts.key_idea: Farming encompasses targeted commercial sectors raising silkworms, fish, grapes, or fruits and flowers.
question_patterns: define sericulture, pisciculture, viticulture, and horticulture
match each specialized cultivation term with its correct description
what is meant by commercial rearing of silkworms
identify the branch of agriculture concerned with growing grapes
distinguish between pisciculture and horticulture

solution_steps.action: Identify the target organism or crop being cultivated
solution_steps.explain: Determine if the activity involves silkworms, fish, grapes, or commercial flowers and fruits.

solution_steps.action: Map to the specific agricultural term
solution_steps.explain: Match silkworms to sericulture, fish to pisciculture, grapes to viticulture, and commercial plants to horticulture.

concepts.title: The Farm System
concepts.definition: An agricultural enterprise functions as a system comprising physical and human inputs, field operations, and harvested yield outputs.
concepts.key_idea: Inputs such as seeds and machinery are transformed through farming operations like ploughing into outputs like crops.
question_patterns: describe the main inputs, processes, and outputs of a farm system
list the physical and human inputs required in agriculture
identify the operational processes involved in crop cultivation
explain how agriculture functions as an input-output system
what are the end outputs produced by an arable farm system

solution_steps.action: Categorize farm system components into inputs, processes, and outputs
solution_steps.explain: Identify physical factors and seeds as inputs, field work as processes, and final produce as outputs.

solution_steps.action: Explain the operational flow of the farming system
solution_steps.explain: Detail how labor and machinery apply processes like sowing and harvesting to transform inputs into agricultural outputs.

concepts.title: Intensive Subsistence Farming
concepts.definition: A farming practice where small landholdings are cultivated using basic tools and abundant manual labor to maximize yield for local consumption.
concepts.key_idea: Dense populations utilize high labor and fertile land to harvest multiple crops annually on small plots.
question_patterns: explain the key characteristics of intensive subsistence agriculture
identify the main crops grown under intensive subsistence farming
which climatic and soil conditions support intensive subsistence farming
distinguish intensive subsistence farming from commercial farming
what regions of the world predominantly practice intensive subsistence farming

solution_steps.action: Outline landholding size and labor requirements
solution_steps.explain: Note that small plot sizes combined with intensive manual household labor characterize this farming type.

solution_steps.action: Identify primary crops and geographic distribution
solution_steps.explain: Recognize rice as the primary crop grown across densely populated monsoon regions of Asia.

concepts.title: Primitive Subsistence Agriculture
concepts.definition: Traditional agricultural methods including shifting land cultivation and seasonal livestock herding tailored to natural environmental conditions.
concepts.key_idea: Shifting cultivation relies on forest clearing and burning while nomadic herding depends on seasonal migrations for pasture.
question_patterns: explain how shifting cultivation is carried out and state its disadvantages
describe nomadic herding and the environmental factors influencing it
what are the regional names for shifting cultivation across the world
identify why land is abandoned in slash and burn agriculture
compare shifting cultivation with nomadic herding

solution_steps.action: Describe the operational mechanics of primitive farming practices
solution_steps.explain: Detail land clearing by burning for shifting cultivation or movement along established routes for herding.

solution_steps.action: Identify environmental constraints and local terminology
solution_steps.explain: Associate slash-and-burn with tropical forest areas and nomadic migration with arid lands, noting regional names like Jhumming or Roca.

concepts.title: Commercial Farming Systems
concepts.definition: Large-scale agricultural production using substantial capital investments and advanced machinery to cultivate crops and raise livestock for market trade.
concepts.key_idea: Commercial agriculture targets market sales through mechanized grain farming, mixed farming, or single-crop plantations.
question_patterns: explain what commercial farming is and name its main types
describe plantation agriculture and its key requirements
what are the features of commercial grain farming in temperate grasslands
distinguish between mixed farming and plantation agriculture
identify major worldwide plantation crops and their growing regions

solution_steps.action: Analyze the commercial objective and mechanization level
solution_steps.explain: Recognize high capital deployment, large land tracts, and machine use focused on market sales.

solution_steps.action: Differentiate between grain, mixed, and plantation sub-types
solution_steps.explain: Identify grain farming in temperate grasslands, mixed crop-livestock farming, and tropical single-crop plantations.

concepts.title: Major Food Crops
concepts.definition: Staple dietary grains—rice, wheat, millets, and maize—grown under specific combinations of temperature, rainfall, and soil conditions.
concepts.key_idea: Food crops demand specialized growing conditions: rice needs water-retentive clay, wheat needs loamy soil, and millets suit arid terrain.
question_patterns: describe the climatic and soil requirements for growing rice and wheat
what are millets and in what geographical conditions do they thrive
compare the growing conditions required for maize and wheat
identify the leading global producers of rice and wheat
list the geographical factors favoring rice cultivation in West Bengal

solution_steps.action: Identify crop-specific temperature, moisture, and soil needs
solution_steps.explain: Match high temperature and alluvial clay with rice, moderate climate and loamy soil with wheat, and low rainfall with coarse millets.

solution_steps.action: State leading global producer nations for each grain
solution_steps.explain: Highlight major producers such as China and India for rice, and USA, Canada, and India for wheat.

concepts.title: Fibre and Beverage Crops
concepts.definition: Industrial and plantation crops supplying natural fibers (cotton, jute) and popular beverages (coffee, tea) requiring distinct physical environments.
concepts.key_idea: Cotton needs frost-free sunshine, jute needs humid tropical heat, while coffee and tea demand well-drained slopes.
question_patterns: state the growth conditions needed for cotton and jute
why is jute known as the golden fibre
explain the geographical requirements for tea and coffee plantations
identify top producing countries for cotton, jute, coffee, and tea
distinguish between the geographical conditions required for coffee and tea

solution_steps.action: Detail physical requirements for fibre crops
solution_steps.explain: Note that cotton needs 210 frost-free days and black soil, while jute requires heavy rain and tropical humidity.

solution_steps.action: Detail physical requirements for beverage crops
solution_steps.explain: Note that coffee thrives on warm loamy hill slopes, whereas tea requires cool climates and evenly distributed rainfall.

concepts.title: Agricultural Development and Food Security
concepts.definition: Programmatic improvements in farming infrastructure, technology, and inputs aimed at expanding output to guarantee population food security.
concepts.key_idea: Modernizing seeds, irrigation, and machinery ensures continuous access to affordable and nutritious food.
question_patterns: define agricultural development and state its primary goal
what is food security and how is it maintained
list the various methods used to increase agricultural production
explain the role of mechanization and high yielding seed varieties in farming
how does agricultural growth contribute to national food security

solution_steps.action: Identify key strategies for agricultural development
solution_steps.explain: List techniques including HYV seed adoption, improved irrigation, chemical inputs, multi-cropping, and mechanization.

solution_steps.action: Connect agricultural growth to food security goals
solution_steps.explain: Explain that boosting farm efficiency ensures all individuals have reliable physical and economic access to safe food.

concepts.title: Comparative Farm Case Study - India versus USA
concepts.section: A Farm in India / A Farm in the USA
concepts.definition: A comparative analysis contrasting small-scale, labor-intensive Indian subsistence holdings with large-scale, automated American commercial farm businesses.
concepts.key_idea: Indian farming focuses on small holdings for subsistence while US farming operates as large-scale scientific business enterprises.
question_patterns: compare the farming practices of a small farmer in India with a commercial farmer in the USA
what are the main differences in farm size between Indian and US agriculture
explain how technology and soil testing are used on a farm in the USA
distinguish between the lifestyle and operations of Indian and American farmers
why are US farmers described as businessmen rather than traditional peasants

solution_steps.action: Contrast farm sizes and operational objectives
solution_steps.explain: Compare small Indian farms (about 1.5 hectares) focused on family yield with massive US holdings (250-300 hectares) focused on market trade.

solution_steps.action: Contrast technological usage and management style
solution_steps.explain: Highlight traditional or rented machinery in India versus satellite-linked scientific management and full automation in the USA.

concepts.title: Estimation of Agricultural Population
concepts.definition: Calculating the total number of individuals dependent on farming by multiplying the total regional population by the agricultural engagement percentage.
concepts.key_idea: Agricultural population equals total population times the percentage engaged in farming divided by one hundred.
question_patterns: calculate the agricultural population given the total population and percentage engaged in farming
find how many people depend on agriculture when the total population is known
determine the number of agricultural workers from population size and agricultural percentage
compute the farming dependent population from total regional population
what is the agricultural population if the total population and engagement rate are given

solution_steps.action: multiply total population by agricultural percentage
solution_steps.explain: find the raw product of total population and percentage

solution_steps.action: divide by 100 to get agricultural population
solution_steps.explain: convert percentage product to absolute head count
